# Team 5 (Accounts, Library, Proposals & Public API) batch — cold review

**Reviewer:** Claude Sonnet 5, orchestrating. Generated by `qwen3.8:27b` via `run_team5_batch.py`
(all five prior fixes plus three new ones added after the Team 4 review: a sharpened no-echo
rule with a named example, a strengthened self-check line, and a quote-diversity rule), 10
tasks, ~19 minutes wall-clock (`_batch.log`). This is the fifth and final team batch. This
review reads every generated file directly against the real `ts5` source tree — both the Astro
frontend and, for the first time, the FastAPI backend and the `ttod_core`/`cli.py` Python
layer — and live `ttod.yml`.
**Date:** 2026-09-11

## Verdict

**Promotable, after real fixes applied in this review.** The module-crossing risk this batch's
own driver prompt was built to guard against — confusing the real, existing
`POST /api/v1/oracle/propose` (Team 3's "propose from answer") with this team's own, not-yet-built
"propose a quote" endpoint — did not occur once across all 10 sheets; the explicit
`critical_disambiguation` block held completely. So did the sibling-scope self-check (zero leaks,
a first for any batch) and the path-discipline rule (zero wrong-file citations, across the widest,
most cross-layer module scope of any team). But three other things went wrong: one factual
hallucination about the real backend's own token mechanism, one fabricated lesson URL, and by far
the worst quote-diversity failure of the whole project.

## What was checked

1. **Wrong-endpoint disambiguation (this batch's own specific, engineered risk) — held.** Task 3
   ("the propose-a-quote backend endpoint") correctly proposes a *new* `POST /api/v1/proposals`
   route calling the real `create_proposal` (`ttod_core/proposals.py:251`) and never once mentions
   `/api/v1/oracle/propose`. Confirmed by direct grep across the batch: zero occurrences.
2. **Path grounding across three layers** — Astro frontend (`auth.server.ts`, `domain.ts`,
   `account/*.astro`), FastAPI backend (`app/auth.py`, `app/main.py`), and the Python CLI layer
   (`ttod_core/proposals.py`, `cli.py`) were all cited only from the real tree, no drift onto a
   sibling module. `cli.py`'s exact line numbers (276, 300, 361) and `domain.ts:80`'s
   `FavoriteEntry` shape were independently re-verified and are accurate.
3. **Sibling-scope discipline — zero leaks, a first.** Read all 7 full sheets against every other
   item's title, per the strengthened rule added after Team 4's item-1-into-item-5 leak. Task 3
   explicitly hands the reviewer queue off to Task 4 ("handled by Task 4"); Task 4 explicitly
   treats the PR/diff mechanics as already-documented, operated not rebuilt; Task 6 explicitly
   documents existing endpoints "rather than inventing new backend routes." No task restated
   another's title as its own success criterion.
4. **A real factual hallucination, found and fixed.** Task 5 claimed `AuthService` has a
   `create_token` method that "generates a JWT" — **neither is true**. The real method is
   `issue_pat(user)`, and it signs a payload with `itsdangerous`'s `URLSafeTimedSerializer` (a
   timed, signed token), not a JWT — confirmed by reading `auth.py` directly. This is the first
   hallucinated API surface (as opposed to a wrong path) in any batch: a plausible-sounding method
   name and technology that simply do not exist in the code. The error repeated four times within
   the same file (worked example, visible result, a "what has to be done" step, and a test-shape
   caveat) — all four **fixed by hand**, replaced with the real `issue_pat`/`read_pat` method
   names and the accurate "signed token, not a JWT" description.
5. **A fabricated, self-flagged lesson URL — the first of its kind.** Task 4's curriculum map
   linked `unit-3-ssr-auth`, a URL the sheet's own text called "hypothetical link structure...
   verify against live site" — and then presented as a clickable link anyway. Checked directly
   (`curl` against the real site): 404. Every other batch's "no unit link exists yet" cases said so
   plainly without inventing a URL; this is the first case of inventing one while self-admitting
   uncertainty. **Fixed by hand**: replaced with the real `unit-3-astro-advanced` link (the same
   one every team's own task 1 already cites).
6. **Meta-instruction echo — recurred a third time, on the same sentence, despite a named
   counter-example.** This batch's `NO_ECHO_RULE` explicitly quoted the Team 4 leak as a
   negative example of exactly what not to write. Task 5 reproduced a close paraphrase of that
   same sentence anyway. Likely explanation: showing the model the bad sentence as an example may
   prime reproduction of similar phrasing rather than suppress it — a plausible, specific failure
   mode worth remembering rather than repeating the same fix pattern next time. **Fixed by hand**;
   folded the genuine Unit 5 link into the oral-defense bullet where it belonged.
7. **Quote citation integrity** — every distinct id (`arch-001`, `qa-014`, `arch-010`, plus the
   six swapped in during this review: `arch-051`, `arch-004`, `arch-013`, `arch-027`, `arch-015`,
   `qa-001`) checked by script against live `ttod.yml`: all real, all exact text matches, all
   present in the 69-quote accounts pool. Zero citation hallucinations — this discipline has now
   held clean across all five batches without a single exception, the whole project through.
8. **Quote repetition — the worst of any batch, by a wide margin, fixed.** As generated:
   `arch-001` cited in **8 of 10 tasks** (1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 7, 8, 9). The `QUOTE_DIVERSITY_RULE` added
   specifically for this batch — requiring any 3rd+ reuse to be named explicitly in the connecting
   paragraph ("this is the Nth use because...") — did not prevent a single one of the eight uses,
   and none of the connecting paragraphs acknowledged the repetition at all. A soft instruction is
   confirmed, now across two consecutive batches, not sufficient to prevent a strongly-fitting
   quote from becoming a default. **Fixed by hand**: reassigned six of the eight uses to distinct,
   individually-grounded alternatives (`arch-051` for the SSR guard-timing task, `arch-004` for the
   favorites/corpus separation, `arch-013` for the create_proposal reuse, `arch-027` for the
   two-touchpoint review pipeline, `arch-015` for session-vs-bearer credential separation, `qa-001`
   for the tests task). Kept `arch-001` only for tasks 8 and 9 (open a PR / review a PR into
   another module) — the one pairing where the quote's own subject (module boundaries) *is*
   literally the task's subject, the same judgment call Team 1's batch independently made for the
   identical pair. Final tally: one pair at 2×, everything else 1× — the cleanest distribution of
   any batch.
9. **Header line, `## Closing` heading, orphan scope** — all present and correct on every sheet;
   this batch's own `team5_tasks.json` upfront check found zero orphaned module scope (the only
   team, besides Content, with none), and nothing surfaced that contradicted that check.

## Disposition

Promoted out of `_draft-team5/` into `docs/DEV_PLAN/ASSIGNMENTS/` proper (10 files,
`ASSIGNMENT-accounts-task1.md` through `task10.md`). Not published to `docs/public/` or the `ts5`

## All five teams now complete

Content (9/9), Graph (10/10), Oracle (10/10), PWA (10/10), Accounts (10/10) — 49 task sheets
total across `docs/DEV_PLAN/ASSIGNMENTS/`, every one cold-reviewed against real source and live
`ttod.yml`, none published to the site yet. Cross-batch findings worth carrying into whatever
uses this skill next (a re-run to regenerate a team, or a similar forger for a different
curriculum):

- **Path/endpoint discipline and sibling-scope self-checks are now validated across five
  independent module domains with the failure rate trending to zero** (one leak in ten batches,
  Team 4's, itself fixed and reinforced) — these two rules are load-bearing and should be kept in
  any future reuse of this pattern.
- **Quote-diversity soft instructions do not reliably work.** Two consecutive batches (Team 4,
  Team 5) produced heavy over-concentration on one or two quotes despite an explicit
  already-used list and, in Team 5's case, an explicit instruction to name and justify any 3rd+
  reuse. If this pattern is reused again, enforce the cap mechanically in the driver (reject and
  re-prompt on a 3rd use rather than asking the model to self-regulate) rather than trying a
  fourth phrasing of the same soft rule.
- **Negative examples in a no-echo rule may backfire.** Naming the exact leaked sentence from a
  prior batch as "don't write this" did not prevent Team 5 from writing a close paraphrase of that
  same sentence — plausibly because showing the bad text primes similar phrasing rather than
  suppressing it. Worth testing a purely rule-based phrasing (no quoted bad example) if this
  pattern recurs a fourth time.
- **Hallucinations do happen, rarely, and take a different shape than expected.** Every prior
  batch's real defects were about paths or scope; this batch produced the project's first
  hallucinated *API surface* (a plausible method name and a wrong underlying technology). Nothing
  in the driver specifically guarded against this because nothing had surfaced it yet — the
  general lesson is that cold review must keep reading every specific technical claim against the
  real source on every batch, not relax once a class of defect stops recurring.

## Addendum (2026-09-11, same day) — the real FE I source, supplied and applied

The user supplied the real FE I "Framework-mode auth lesson" reference —
[HELIOS DECK's architecture](https://ruvebal.github.io/web-atelier-udit/tracks/es/geo-physical-aggregator/arch/)
— confirming it as canonical ("this is law"). Fetched and checked directly, rather than assumed:
it documents `requireUser(request)` reading the session in a *loader*, before render, redirecting
to `/auth/login` if unauthenticated, backed by an `HttpOnly` `createCookieSessionStorage` cookie.
It does **not** mention `requireRole` or `tokenStorage.js` at all — both are TTOD's own
extensions on top of the base FE I lesson, not things FE I itself taught.

This resolved three "not yet published" gaps this review had left open, all now fixed by hand:

- **Task 1** previously cited "FE I Framework-mode auth lesson" as a bare, unlinked phrase, and
  slightly overclaimed that FE I itself taught `requireUser`/`requireRole` together. Fixed: real
  link added, and the sheet now explicitly says role-gating is TTOD's own extension, not
  inherited curriculum.
- **Task 4** previously linked `unit-3-astro-advanced` as a fallback (itself a repair, in this
  same review, of a fabricated `unit-3-ssr-auth` URL) — a real but only tangentially-relevant
  substitute, since that unit is about content collections and i18n, not auth. Fixed: replaced
  with the real, precisely on-topic HELIOS DECK link.
- **Task 6** previously asserted the FE I lesson covers "the separation of session and bearer
  tokens" as one lesson. Fixed: the real source only covers the session half — the sheet now says
  so explicitly, rather than implying FE I already taught the two-credential distinction TTOD
  actually originates.

Task 5's own `tokenStorage.js` citation (a different, bearer-token-specific FE I concept, sourced
from the real `auth/ASSIGNMENT.md`'s own "FE I map" table, not from this URL) was left unchanged —
this specific page does not cover it, so linking it there would have been a new mismatch of the
same kind just fixed elsewhere.
